items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: the regular rhythm section consists of White Newman piano, Lawrence Morale banjo, Eddie Morale bass, and myself drums.

ctx.x: I'll leave this over there on tip on that. All right. That's all right. You can't hear it. You're talking about Bebe originally. Yeah, you know. And Papa Celestan.

Well, that time he used to...that we had the original Tuxedo Band. And then we used the title of the Young Tuxedo Band. Now that outfit consists of Dwight Newman on piano, and we had trained over to Paul Bent on trombone, Dennis Harris on saxophone and clarinet, Louis Contrell on saxophone and tenor sax and clarinet. And the regular rhythm section consists of White Newman piano, Lawrence Morale banjo, Eddie Morale bass, and myself drums. That was the regular rhythm. Eight pieces out.
What kind of a drum set did you get in the beginning?

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: And then we just add two more men stood. That's by adding a piano, a fella by the name of Dwight Newman.

ctx.x: Yeah. Still a sad man? Yeah, majority of the same men, yeah. Yeah. We made that band into the Young Tuxedo Band. And then we just add two more men stood. That's by adding a piano, a fella by the name of Dwight Newman.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: That's the Creole Serenades. Henry Martin on drum, Dwight Newman on piano, Andrew Bocard, Charlie Bocard, and Peter Bocard.

ctx.x: He quit the old band, Pierron did, and that's up, that's called Peter Bocard, and then they made up another group they called the Creole Serenades. Mm-hmm. You see, that's the picture you've got now. Oh yeah. That's the Creole Serenades. Henry Martin on drum, Dwight Newman on piano, Andrew Bocard, Charlie Bocard, and Peter Bocard.
Oh, let me ask you about another band that we don't have much information on. Do you remember anything about the Nola band? Oh yeah, Peter Bocard, yeah. Who was in that band? Who was in that band?
